mechanism_narrative: A CPIAUCSL value above 220 (as of 2016-10) indicates persistent inflation that triggers Federal Reserve tightening expectations, increasing equity discount rates and reducing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 220, or the Rank IC between CPIAUCSL and 20-day returns is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 0.5% signals active monetary tightening, increasing borrowing costs and reducing corporate profitability, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 0.5%, or the Rank IC between FEDFUNDS and 20-day returns is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in PAYEMS and decreases in UNRATE indicate an overheating labor market that accelerates inflation and triggers monetary tightening, reducing S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS is above 12-month average and UNRATE is below 12-month average, or the Rank IC between the interaction term and 20-day returns is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion (UNRATE < 5.0%), the economy approaches peak growth, increasing recession risk and reducing corporate earnings, which causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE < 5.0%, or the Rank IC between UNRATE and 20-day returns in late-cycle periods is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts below 480 thousand units signal weak residential construction, reducing consumer demand and corporate revenue growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when HOUST < 480, or the Rank IC between HOUST and 20-day returns is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production below 93.0 (index 2017=100) indicates manufacturing contraction, reducing corporate output and profits, which causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO < 93.0, or the Rank IC between INDPRO and 20-day returns is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Persistent CPIAUCSL above 220 (as of 2016-10) indicates sustained inflation that increases medium-term monetary tightening risk, reducing S&P 500 valuations and causing negative returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 220, or the Rank IC between CPIAUCSL and 60-day returns is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Retail and food services sales below 389,000 million dollars indicate weak consumer spending, reducing corporate revenue growth and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when RSAFS < 389000, or the Rank IC between RSAFS and 5-day returns is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.
